text:
I understand it's during COVID, but the doctor went too far. They showed blatant disgust, constantly telling me to stay away and to stay right there. When it came time to pay, they refused cash and pointed for me to scan a QR code.
I wonder what people who don't have internet access would do?
The doctor was excessive. I was wearing a mask and everything was proper protection. They even asked what vaccine dose I had received. When I said I'd had two, they told me to go to a vaccination booth. I want to say that getting vaccinated is a personal right. Some people are afraid of getting sick.
Their disgust was too obvious. We're all human beings. The doctor even told me to stay away from their area. If you don't truly care about treating fellow human beings, don't bother going into this profession. (This was just to get a medical certificate.)
**You can be disgusted by the disease, but don't be disgusted by your fellow human beings.**

restaurant_name: คลินิกสุขภาพชุมชน
text:
If you are sick or unwell, we do not recommend going to this clinic. Because you will only get sicker (mentally).
The story is, I wanted to get tested for diabetes, but my job requires me to sleep early and wake up late. I had researched that the requirement for a diabetes test is to fast for 8 hours. Before the test, I had already fasted for 11-12 hours, from 5 am to 4 pm. But the clinic refused to test me, saying that it wouldn't give accurate blood sugar readings. They said I had to fast from midnight to 8 am before the test.
I explained why I couldn't fast at midnight, why I couldn't come at 8 am, because I work a night shift, etc. (But they kept interrupting me while I was explaining, like they weren't listening).
The clinic then said that I had to fast from midnight to 8 am like everyone else. If I couldn't do it like everyone else, it was okay. (The phrase "it's okay" felt like being fired. And what does "everyone else" even mean? Do I have two sets of teeth that I'm not a normal person?)
In summary... But the truth is, getting the actual information was a headache. I asked the same questions four or five times because they wouldn't listen. I felt like I was talking to a rap artist. Basically, whatever your life is like, if you want to get tested, you have to fast from midnight to 8 AM. It doesn't matter if you've already gone without sleep and food, it has to be during this time. The clinic said this is the standard international standard for diabetes testing.
*****My reason for posting this is: Is it true that internationally recognized diabetes testing requires fasting from midnight to 8 AM only, because the clinic said it has to be during this time? Or is this specific to this clinic only?*******
I apologize for my lack of knowledge. If anyone knows, please tell me so I don't misunderstand the clinic. And I want to tell the clinic to learn to listen to patients, otherwise they'll get kicked in the ass. (The person I spoke to seemed to be a healthcare worker, not a staff member.)
P.S. I'm not calling them a doctor or physician because they lack credibility and respect.
